quotes.text: If your data isn't indexed and permissioned inside the Microsoft Graph, it effectively does not exist to your AI. We have to move beyond the phase of just chatting with a PDF.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis in one sentence.

quotes.text: Integrated is not the same as indexed. An integration might let you see a CRM record inside Outlook, but that doesn't mean the AI can reason across it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a crisp distinction that many organizations overlook.

quotes.text: Your connector must replicate the source permissions with absolute fidelity. If a user can't see a record in the original SQL database, they must not see it in a copilot response.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear security rule for building connectors.

quotes.text: Every custom connector you build needs more than just a developer. It needs a business owner. This person is responsible for the quality standard and the life cycle policy of that data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical governance advice on connector ownership.

quotes.text: Identify the one system where missing context is currently causing the most rework. Don't try to boil the ocean. Find one high-impact connector.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Copilot grounded only in SharePoint and OneDrive documents misses the live system state, such as approvals, tickets and exceptions, that drives real business decisions.
Custom Graph connectors bring that external context into the semantic index, but only if identities, schema, ACL-based security trimming and latency targets are designed deliberately.
Treat every connector as a governed business asset with a named owner, respect data residency, and start with the one system whose missing context causes the most rework.
hook: Your Copilot answers sound confident, but they are built on only a fraction of your business: the documents in SharePoint and OneDrive. This episode is for Microsoft 365 architects and IT leaders who want AI that sees approvals, tickets and exceptions living in external systems, and shows how Graph connectors, permissions and governance turn a blind assistant into a real-time business brain.
